title: Simulation study on flow field and total noise of a segmented ducted fan for small UAVs, Vehicles 2026
version: Vehicles 8(7):165, gold OA; full text HTTP 403 from mdpi.com to this client on 2026-09-12 (bot protection; not circumvented)
evidence_grade: C (CFD-only per its own abstract; abstract cannot establish detailed negatives)
finding: The closest competitor by name. 'Segmented' here means AXIAL duct spacing (0-20 mm gaps between duct sections along the axis) studied by CFD (k-omega SST + broadband noise model) at 20,000-40,000 rpm; the paper reports acoustic power rising with spacing and recommends <=10 mm. It is not circumferential seams at equal mean radial clearance, it is simulation only with no measurement, the geometry is fixed (no deployment), and the abstract states it cannot resolve transients. It must be cited and distinguished explicitly: same word, different geometry.

axes.equal_mean_clearance_discrete_seams: discussed: axial segmentation gaps, not circumferential seams at equal mean clearance
axes.matched_controls: integral duct as comparator, per abstract

title: High-sensitive fibre sensor for tip clearance measurements in a turbine rig, Sensors 2018
locator: Abstract; Introduction (TC typically <3 mm, resolution better than 25 um required; capacitive/eddy-current/microwave alternatives); sensor design and calibration sections
evidence_grade: B for the instrument; not an aerodynamic study
finding: Fibre-bundle reflective sensor, ~2 mm range about 3.2 mm standoff, sensitivity 61.73 mm^-1, operated in a turbine rig. Confirms that sub-25 um per-location clearance measurement is an established capability, i.e. measuring the mean clearance and the per-seam deviation independently is feasible with existing sensors; this bears on the matched-control axis (mean clearance can be verified, not assumed equal).

axes.matched_controls: supports: mean clearance is measurable to <25 um so 'equal mean' can be verified
